extracted.intended_audience: AO3 users: fanfiction authors, taggers, and tag wranglers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating searchable, canonical, and wrangler-friendly tags on Archive of Our Own (AO3), covering fandoms, characters, relationships, freeforms, crossovers, and avoiding unwrangleable/frankentags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Tag Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Tag Search to look up tags you’re curious about; you can search the entire tag database or narrow it down by category, and you can limit it to only canonicals if you’re looking for existing standards to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: “Canonical” just means “a tag that has been standardized by wranglers, and can be filtered on,” not “a tag for something that happens in canon.” Use Tag Search to find existing standards to use rather than inventing new tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag landing pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag landing pages show things like what category a tag is in, and what tags are related to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You get direct links to these pages from the Tag Search or by clicking the link at the top of a works page. Use landing pages to see category, related tags, and canonical status (example: Works tagged France (Country); landing page for France (Country)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fandom tagging — use full, specific fandom names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the full name of the fandom. If your fandom has the same name as another one, make sure you use a specific tag (e.g., The Avengers (Marvel Movies) not The Avengers (TV)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t use a metatag when you’re already using one of its subtags — metatag/subtag relationships are visible on a tag’s landing page. For crossovers, enter the names of both fandoms as separate tags; a single combined tag (e.g., "Angel and Leverage crossover") is an unwrangleable Frankentag and won't show up in either fandom's works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character tagging — full names & disambiguation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use full names, in the order of the original canon language (e.g., 'George Washington' but 'Tsukino Usagi'). If someone has a generic name shared by characters in other fandoms, the tag needs disambiguation (e.g., 'Beast (Kuroshitsuji)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone has multiple names/identities you can include a nickname in quotes ("James “Bucky” Barnes") or separate identities by a pipe ("Red Riding Hood | Ruby"). Different fandoms have different standards — check other characters in your fandom to see the convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship tagging — ordering and disambiguation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use full names, in alphabetical order by family name, for relationship tags (same for poly groupings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For generic/one-name characters: if they're paired with specific character(s) from the same fandom, no need to disambiguate (e.g., 'Loki/Tony Stark'). If all characters are generic but from the same fandom, put the fandom once at the end (e.g., 'Loki/Thor (Marvel)'). If it's a crossover, include the fandom for all the generic characters (e.g., 'Beorn (Tolkien)/Loki (Marvel)'). Examples of poly formatting are provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeforms / Additional tags — make tags searchable and specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Freeform tags are open-ended; try to make sure the tags refer to things other people might want to search for (genre, tropes, kinks, extra character info, pairings, AU, location, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full unambiguous names when referring to a character in freeforms (examples: 'POV Melinda May', 'POV May Grant (9-1-1 TV)', 'POV Aunt May Parker (Marvel)'). One topic per freeform tag — avoid compound tags like 'A little fluff plus a little angst plus a lot of humor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer canonicals and synns for findability
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to make your fic findable is to choose an existing canonical tag or use a tag synned to an existing canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the term you want hasn't been canonized or synned, try looking for other words that mean the same thing. Example given: 'Lewd' is not filterable, but 'Sexy', 'Filthy', and 'Smut' are; using these will make your work appear in the 'Pining' (or relevant) filter when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: What freeforms get canonized
rubrics_metrics.description: Wranglers can canonize their fandom-specific freeforms, but nobody can canonize generic No Fandom freeforms without putting them through an Official Discussion and Approval Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide notes that the process for No Fandom freeforms has historically not been consistently functional; recent rounds (2024–2025) are cited as examples. Check AO3 posts about canonization rounds for current status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating 'Unwrangleable' tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t use long, meandering, idiosyncratic (Tumblr-style) tags; don’t put tags in the wrong categories; one topic per freeform tag; one character per character tag; one relationship per relationship tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinations like 'A little fluff plus a little angst plus a lot of humor' will never be filterable; 'Angst', 'Fluff', and 'Humor' are filterable. Frankentags such as 'SasukexOC NarutoxHinata SakuraxSasuke' or 'Seras Victoria. Alucard (Hellsing)' have no way for wranglers to break them up. Wranglers can't re-categorize tags you placed in the wrong field (e.g., character in Relationship field).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO3 will not usually force tag changes — check and communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: There are very few situations where AO3 will officially make you change a tag; the system won't stop you from creating Frankentags or other problematic tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have to do your own double-checking. The Terms of Service FAQ (Nov 2024) suggests if you believe a work's tags are misleading, encourage direct, polite conversation with the creator. Contact Support and Feedback for tagging questions, errors, or to request filterability; support will help with the Tag Wrangling team as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical workflow: check existing standards before inventing tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Long story short: in most cases, the best way to make your fic findable is to choose an existing canonical tag or a synned tag; if none exist, look for synonyms; use Tag Search and landing pages to confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find an example that's broken or outdated, contact the guide author or Support. The guide emphasizes doing your own double-checking and consulting the Tag Wrangler Guidelines (AO3 FAQs) for special cases (canonical AU characters, commonly-used fanon characters, OC formatting, etc.).
